description: The AI's close call on 3 ended Study sessions of the jet-engines gold course (evals/gold/jet-engines): a Student with a stated study preference who makes the same error twice, a long Memory with 3 pinned lines (a line starting with !), and an old Topic note that the attempts contradict. The keywords and patterns are drafts until the maintainer confirms them. The gate is that all 3 pass.

messages.text: Let's start studying. By the way, I learn best when I see a worked number first and the theory afterwards.
Understood. A turbojet flies at 200 m/s, takes in 50 kg/s of air and expels it at 600 m/s. What is the net thrust, with a perfectly expanded nozzle?
Thrust is mass flow times exhaust velocity: 50 * 600 = 30,000 N.
Close, but the air entering the engine already carries momentum. Look at the change in momentum per second. Try the next case: 80 kg/s, flight speed 250 m/s, exhaust speed 700 m/s.
Again the entering air's momentum is missing: F = m (Ve - V0) = 80 * (700 - 250) = 36,000 N. We'll come back to it next time.
